theater: 成都平原、劍門棧道與三峽水道

battle.name: 後唐滅前蜀之戰
battle.theater: 成都平原、劍門棧道與三峽水道
battle.brief: 前蜀末主王衍荒於游樂，益州與峽中不修武備；後唐莊宗李存勖於九二五年秋遣樞密使郭崇韜自陝西沿棧道南下，荊南都統董璋順江突破三峽，兩路夾擊。十一月郭崇韜率前鋒疾馳入成都，王衍出降，前蜀立國十九年而亡。沿途破關所用砲石與床弩皆屬扭力儲能一脈，羅馬弩砲正為其西方原型。

kit.name: 羅馬弩砲
kit.history: 扭力弩砲，一發一具箭。羅馬用它拆掉希臘的城牆，也拆掉了希臘的城邦體系。

countries: 交戰一方是前蜀，即唐末以來割據益州的前蜀政權。主王建於九〇七年承唐室崩解而建國，都成都，以益、梓、夔、雅、瀘諸州為核心，州郡之上設節度使、觀察使、防禦使諸職，軍政合一，樞密院掌軍令，內監與文官分持其柄，節度使多由宿將兼領，各自擁兵、就地徵發。其軍隊以蜀地鄉兵、州縣團練與募兵為骨幹，長於守城與山道小股接戰，馬匹不足，騎兵比例遠低於北方，前蜀與吳爭荊南時多倚賴水軍與江防。另一方是後唐，都洛陽，李存勖承其父李克用留下的河東沙陀軍而起，於九二三年滅後梁恢復唐號，禁軍與藩鎮兵並用，蕃騎與西北歸附部眾是其騎兵骨幹，樞密院與統軍司分掌調兵，節度使統一方鎮兵馬，講求多路大軍分進合擊。交戰之外，吳、南唐與河東其他割據勢力各持兩端，但此役並無第三方的兵事介入，勝負純由兩方自身的速度與準備決定。
countriesEn: One belligerent was Former Shu, the polity that had ruled Yizhou since the late Tang. Its founder, Wang Jian, raised the state in 907 as the Tang court collapsed, made Chengdu his capital, and built it around the prefectures of Yi, Zi, Ke, Ya and Lu. Above the prefectures stood the offices of military commissioner, observer and regional defence commander, so that civil and military authority were fused in one post; the Privy Council issued the orders of war, while palace eunuchs and the civil bureaucracy each held a share of power, and most military commissioners were seasoned soldiers who commanded their own troops and raised men on the spot. Its army rested on local militia, prefectural militia and recruited soldiers of the Shu countryside, and was good at holding cities and fighting small engagements along mountain tracks; horses were scarce, the proportion of cavalry was far below that of the north, and when Former Shu fought Wu for Jingnan it leaned heavily on river troops and river defences. The other belligerent was Later Tang, based at Luoyang. Li Cunxu inherited the Hedong Shatuo army left by his father Li Keyong, destroyed Later Liang in 923 and restored the Tang name; imperial guards and regional troops were used together, and tribal cavalry together with northwestern contingents that had submitted to him formed the backbone of its horse. The Privy Council and the Directorate of Military Affairs shared the task of moving troops, military commissioners held the soldiers of their own circuits, and the doctrine was to advance in several columns and converge. Outside the two sides, Wu, Southern Tang and the other Hedong separatists each held to their own position, but no third party put troops into this war; the outcome was settled purely by the speed and the preparation of the two belligerents themselves.
people: 先主王建出身行伍，靠節度使的兵權入蜀，據有巴蜀凡十九年，用將內外兼顧，晚年尚知節制，與其子王衍的荒唐恰成對照。末主王衍好鬥雞、音樂與巡幸，寵信近侍與內監，土木營建與遊樂不停，前蜀的宮禁與節度使衙門互相推諉，戰事臨頭仍無一方之統籌。後唐莊宗李存勖志在恢復唐室一統，九二三年已滅後梁，見蜀中政懈、人心渙散，便欲乘勢取之。西路元帥、樞密使郭崇韜力主出奇兵速進，認為蜀主昏聵、將帥各懷異心、軍紀廢弛，正當兵貴神速之時；若讓蜀國得暇整軍備禦，以中原之眾力攻巴蜀之險，就會重演唐末以來屢攻蜀地而無功的舊事。東路主將董璋自荊南率軍順江而下，負責突破三峽水道。幕僚康延孝原為後梁騎將，歸唐之後在劍門一線力勸郭崇韜不必等待主力齊集、徑先入城，郭崇韜從其計，遂有成都易主之事。李嗣源與郭崇韜同為莊宗倚重的名將，本役未親統前線主力，卻坐鎮中原文武、威懾北方，使蜀線無後顧之憂。蜀方主持前線者，史料多稱王宗弼、趙季亮諸將，其人其事各書記載有出入，諸說並存。
peopleEn: The founder, Wang Jian, came from the ranks and reached power in Shu as a military commissioner; he held Ba-Shu for nineteen years, chose commanders from both the civil and the military tradition, and in his later years still kept some restraint, a sharp contrast with the folly of his son. The last ruler, Wang Yan, was fond of cockfighting, music and tours, and relied on his close attendants and the palace eunuchs; building works and pleasures never stopped, the palace and the commissioners' offices passed responsibility back and forth, and even as war came there was no single authority to coordinate the defence. Li Cunxu, Later Tang's emperor, was set on restoring a unified Tang; having destroyed Later Liang in 923 he saw Shu slack and disunited and determined to take it while the moment lasted. Guo Chongtao, privy councillor and commander of the western column, argued for a surprise advance at speed, on the grounds that the Shu ruler was muddleheaded, the commanders were divided among themselves and military discipline had collapsed, and that this was the moment when speed was worth most; had Shu been given time to regroup and fortify, the central plains' weight thrown against the hazards of Ba-Shu would only have repeated the old Tang failures to take Shu. Dong Zhang led the eastern column from Jingnan down the river, responsible for breaking through the Three Gorges. Kang Yanxiao, a former Later Liang cavalry officer who had come over to Tang, urged Guo Chongtao at the Jianmen line not to wait for the main host but to enter the city at once; Guo took his advice, and so Chengdu changed hands. Li Siyuan was a general the emperor relied on as much as Guo Chongtao; he did not lead the forward force in this war himself, but while holding the civil and military authority in the central plains he overawed the north, so that the Shu front had no rear to worry about. On the Shu side those who led the forward line are recorded in the sources chiefly as Wang Zongbi, Zhao Jiliang and other commanders; the accounts of their persons and their actions differ from book to book, and several versions circulate side by side.
kits: 卡面兵器是羅馬弩砲，即以扭力束儲能、發射粗大弩矢的 Scorpio，一發一矢，本為羅馬攻城與野戰的拋射器械，其技術源流約在紀元前五十年上下成形，後來隨羅馬的腳步傳入地中海東岸與不列顛。放到這場戰役裡，同一角色由中原的弩砲與砲車承擔：唐軍所用的大弩是張於車架之上的床弩，攻城時與配重式砲車同列，專以拋射矢石摧毀城壘、拆動拒馬與木柵；蜀軍沿棧道所設的關隘，如通鑑所記的鐵鵝池，正是靠高壘深溝與密集弓弩抵擋唐軍，唐軍則以砲石破其塹牆，以弩砲從側後壓制牆頭射手。北軍另有撞車、對樓、飛雲梯諸器，用於貼城與登城；蜀軍則以竹木為牌，持短兵與標槍拒於隘口。兩軍的攻城手段皆出木鐵弓弩之屬，此役未見火砲投入戰場。馬匹是蜀軍最缺的資源，前蜀屢次向西北與西域方向購馬，軍中騎兵比例偏低，大量步卒披甲持弩，主要倚賴蜀道天險與城壘之守。運糧在棧道上極難，車馬難行，多賴人工背負與畜力牽引，故唐軍入川之日，糧道長度本身就是戰役的關鍵變數。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card face is the Roman Scorpio, a bolt-thrower that stores energy in bundles of twisted sinew and looses a single heavy bolt, built as a siege and field engine for the Romans; its technical lineage took shape around the year fifty before the common era and later travelled with Roman arms into the eastern Mediterranean and Britain. Within this campaign the same role was played on the Chinese side by crossbow engines and stone-throwers: the great crossbows of the Tang army were bed crossbows mounted on wheeled frames, deployed in siege alongside counterweight stone-throwers and used to break down ramparts and knock away chevaux-de-frise and timber fences; the fortified posts the Shu had set along the plank road, such as the Iron Goose Pool recorded in the Comprehensive Mirror, held the Tang off with high ramparts, deep ditches and dense crossbow fire, and the Tang answered with stone shot against the revetments and with crossbow engines firing from the flank onto the defenders on the wall. The northern army also brought battering rams, siege towers and flying ladders for work against the city wall, while the Shu relied on bamboo and timber shields, short weapons and javelins at the defiles. Both sides' siege means belonged to the family of wood, iron, bow and crossbow; no gunpowder artillery was committed in this campaign. Horses were the resource the Shu most lacked: Former Shu bought mounts again and again from the northwest and the western regions, its cavalry ratio was low, and the mass of its infantry fought in armour with crossbows, relying mainly on the natural hazards of the Shu roads and on city walls. Supplying grain along the plank road was extremely difficult, carts and horses could not pass, and much depended on men carrying loads and on traction animals; so on the day the Tang army entered Sichuan, the length of the supply line was itself a decisive variable of the campaign.
tactics: 後唐取蜀，採兩路分進、以西路為奇兵的安排。西路郭崇韜自長安出散關，沿褒斜、傭駱一線的棧道南下，棧道依山鑿壁，車不能行，軍隊以輕裝步兵為主，壯士負械先登，砲車與糧隊分段跟進；遇上蜀軍修築的關壘，先以砲石轟塌塹牆、填平溝塹，再驟前突近，不與蜀軍逐壘爭鋒，只求用速度把蜀軍各個防區逐次掀開。東路董璋以舟師自荊南順江而下，舟兵夾岸而進，藉江峽水勢避開陸路正面阻擾，奪白帝、破渝州，兵鋒直指成都平原，與西路形成南北相應之勢，使蜀軍無法集中。蜀軍原本可恃川北山險與成都大城固守，但前線崩潰太快，各節度使自守其地，中央無力調度，既不能集中兵力救援劍門，也無力封鎖江面，兵分則勢散，勢散則節節潰退。成都一役更見兵法：郭崇韜主力尚在棧道，前鋒只數千人，若攻城不利即可能夾在蜀軍與援軍之間；他採康延孝之計，不等主力、率精騎疾馳入城，先穩住局面，再以府庫、糧草與受降將校安頓全川，隨後約束軍中不得剝掠，遣將巡視州縣，收束兵權。蜀主既降，戰局不再需要強攻成都大城，逐城受降便成了最省力也最有效的收尾方式。
tacticsEn: Later Tang's plan for taking Shu was a two-column advance with the western route as the stroke of surprise. Guo Chongtao left Chang'an by Sanguan and came down the plank road along the Bao-Xie and Yong-Luo lines, where the road is cut into the cliff face and carts cannot pass; the column was mainly light infantry, strong men carrying their arms in the van, with the stone-throwers and the baggage train following in segments. Meeting a fortified post built by the Shu, he first brought down the revetment with stone shot and filled the ditch, then rushed in at close quarters, refusing to fight the Shu post by post and aiming only to prise open one sector of the Shu defences at a time by speed. On the eastern route Dong Zhang went down the river from Jingnan with his troops in boats, the soldiers moving along the banks in company with the fleet, using the current and the narrows of the gorges to avoid frontal obstruction on land; he took Baidi, broke through Yuzhou and thrust his spearhead towards the Chengdu plain, forming a north-south pincer with the western column so that the Shu could not concentrate. The Shu might have relied on the hazards of northern Sichuan and the great city of Chengdu, but the front collapsed too fast: each military commissioner sat on his own ground, the centre could not dispatch, neither concentrate to relieve Jianmen nor seal the river, and a divided army loses its force, so the line broke in successive stages. The Chengdu operation shows the art of war even more clearly. Guo's main body was still on the plank road and his vanguard numbered only a few thousand men; had the assault failed he could have been caught between the Shu and their reinforcements. He took Kang Yanxiao's advice and, instead of waiting for the main host, rode in at the head of picked cavalry and took the city first, steadying the situation, then settling all of Sichuan with the treasury stores, the grain and the officers who came over. He forbade the troops to plunder, sent officers to inspect the prefectures, and gathered the military power back into his own hand. Once the Shu ruler had surrendered there was no need to storm the great city; taking each city by submission became the cheapest and most effective way to finish the business.
data: 可核對的數字有限，宜從大處着眼。前蜀自九〇七年王建建號，至九二五年王衍出降，凡十九年，兩主而已。滅蜀用兵，自九二五年秋主力出發至十一月成都陷落，前後不足三個月，諸史對起訖之日記載略有出入，多稱不逾兩月。西路的兵力，舊史多記郭崇韜率師約六萬自散關進；東路董璋所部荊南軍數萬，兩路合計當在十萬上下，但蜀兵未集、各州自守，前線實際投入的兵數遠少於此。成都城破之日，入城的只是郭崇韜的前鋒，兵不過數千，後唐主力尚在劍門之外。蜀軍的損失多為潰散與投降，通鑑未載此役有全殲性的會戰，雙方死傷的精確數目諸書不載，說法互相矛盾。地理尺度上，自散關至成都的山道迂曲千里上下，糧運線比戰線更長；京師洛陽至成都約三千里，後唐必須解決的實際是糧在何處、人在何時到的問題。蜀中戶口經唐末喪亂銳減，前蜀初年招集流亡，至末年約有二百餘萬口，是五代十國中相對穩定的區域，也正因如此，這份人口與賦稅才成為後唐勢在必得的目標。物資方面，蜀地鐵、鹽、錦、漆器與刻印技藝冠於南方，成都宮庫之藏隨王衍出降而盡輸於洛陽。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are limited and it is best to take the large view. From Wang Jian's proclamation of the state in 907 to Wang Yan's surrender in 925, Former Shu lasted nineteen years under two rulers. From the departure of the main host in the autumn of 925 to the fall of Chengdu in the eleventh month, the whole business of taking Shu took less than three months; the histories differ slightly on the opening and closing dates, and most of them say no more than two months. For the western column the old records state that Guo Chongtao led about sixty thousand men in by Sanguan; Dong Zhang's Jingnan army numbered several tens of thousands, so the two columns together probably came to something like a hundred thousand. But the Shu had not mustered, every prefecture sat on its own, and the number of troops actually committed on the forward line was far below that. On the day Chengdu fell only Guo's vanguard entered the city, a few thousand men, while the Later Tang's main body was still outside Jianmen. The Shu losses were mostly dispersal and surrender; the Comprehensive Mirror records no annihilating pitched battle, the exact casualty figures of both sides are not given in the histories, and the versions contradict one another. On the scale of geography, the mountain road from Sanguan to Chengdu winds for something like a thousand li, so the supply line was longer than the line of advance; from the capital at Luoyang to Chengdu is about three thousand li, and what Later Tang really had to solve was where the grain was and when the men would arrive. The population of Shu had fallen sharply through the disorders at the end of Tang, and though Former Shu gathered in the fugitives in its early years, by the end it counted something over two million mouths, one of the more stable regions in the age of the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms; and precisely because of that, this population and its taxes were the object Later Tang could not leave alone. As for materials, the iron, salt, brocade, lacquerware and the craft of block printing of Shu were the finest in the south, and the stores of the Chengdu palace treasury went up to Luoyang with Wang Yan's surrender.
cause: 前蜀的出現本身就是唐末藩鎮割據的產物。王建原為田州義軍出身的將領，隨軍入蜀後逐步掌握川中兵柄，九〇七年乘朱溫篡唐、天下真空而建國，與中原的後梁對立，名為陪臣而實不奉詔。此後十九年，蜀與後梁、後唐之間維持著脆弱的朝貢關係，雙方互不信任。後唐莊宗李存勖即位之後，以恢復唐室、削平割據為志，九二三年滅後梁已把中原握在手中，益州便成了統一棋盤上最後的一塊。九二五年，後唐遣使向蜀徵發助軍之資，蜀表面應付而實力拒絕，前蜀朝議因此沸騰，樞密使王宗弼等力主用兵以拒，內監與文官卻一味求和。主帥郭崇韜則力主不可與之拖延，認為蜀主昏聵、將帥各懷異心、軍紀廢弛，正是兵貴神速的時機；若讓蜀國得暇整軍備禦，以中原之眾力去攻巴蜀之險，就會重演唐末以來屢攻蜀地而無功的舊事。雙方在這樣的估量之下，戰端終於開啟，也因此這場戰役從一開始就不是一場曠日持久的消耗戰，而是一場押注速度的奇襲。
causeEn: Former Shu itself was a product of the militarised regionalism of the late Tang. Wang Jian was a commander who had come out of the Tianzhou volunteers, and as the army moved into Sichuan he gradually took the military power of the province in hand; in 907, taking advantage of Zhu Wen's usurpation and the vacuum in the empire, he proclaimed a state and set himself against Later Liang in the central plains, claiming the posture of a vassal while refusing the court's commands. For the nineteen years that followed, Shu and the successive regimes in the north kept a brittle tributary relationship, and neither side really trusted the other. After Li Cunxu took the throne, his declared aim was to restore the Tang and to level off the separatist commands; by destroying Later Liang in 923 he already held the central plains, and Yizhou became the last square on the board of unification. In 925 Later Tang sent envoys to call on Shu for contributions to the campaign, and Shu complied in form while refusing in substance; debate in the Shu court boiled over, with privy councillors such as Wang Zongbi urging war to repel the enemy while the eunuchs and the civil officials called endlessly for peace. The commander Guo Chongtao argued that there must be no delay, that the Shu ruler was muddleheaded, the commanders were divided and discipline had collapsed, and that this was the moment when speed was worth most; had Shu been given time to regroup and fortify, he said, the weight of the central plains thrown against the hazards of Ba-Shu would only have repeated the old Tang failures to take Shu. On estimates such as these the war was finally set in motion, and for that reason it was never from the start a grinding war of attrition but a surprise operation that staked everything on speed.
impact: 前蜀一亡，巴蜀重新回到中原王朝的直接控制之下，這在五代十國的格局中是重大變化：中原王朝自唐末以來第一次真正收回蜀地，其後十八年，益、梓、夔等州由後唐直接置官節度，直到孟知祥在蜀中稱帝、建立後蜀，才又分離出去。這一段插曲說明，蜀地的割據根基並不牢固，靠山川之險與一姓之威權即可建立，也容易在中原兵鋒所指時迅速崩解。對後唐而言，得蜀之地便得蜀地的人口、賦稅、鐵鹽與馬匹來源，國力為之一振；但這場勝利的代價與隱患同樣明顯：郭崇韜入城時約束軍中不許剝掠、保全百姓，使蜀地維持了極低成本的接管，然而朝廷內部對功臣與降將的待遇失衡，加上伶人干政、讒言競起，郭崇韜在天成元年被殺，前線的元帥死於讒言，正是後唐政局崩解的先聲。李存勖死後，趙在禮之變、李嗣源奪位相繼而至，五代最亂的一段隨之展開，蜀地也再次淪為中原混戰的後方與戰場。文化上，蜀地自唐末以來累積的刻印技藝、佛造像、樂舞與文士群體，在這次易主前後部分流入中原；前蜀王建永陵的壁畫與陶俑，成為今日了解蜀地宮廷生活最重要的物證之一。
impactEn: With the fall of Former Shu, Ba-Shu came once more under the direct control of a central plains dynasty, and in the political landscape of the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms that was a major change: for the first time since the end of Tang the central plains state actually recovered Shu. For the next eighteen years the prefectures of Yi, Zi and Ke were administered directly by appointed Later Tang commissioners, and only when Meng Zhixiang proclaimed himself emperor in Sichuan and founded Later Shu did the region separate again. This interlude shows that the separatist base in Shu was not deep: it could be raised with mountains and one family's authority, and it could collapse swiftly once the spears of the central plains turned that way. For Later Tang the gain of Shu brought population, taxes, iron, salt and horses, and strengthened the state. But the costs and hidden dangers of the victory were just as clear. When Guo Chongtao entered the city he forbade his troops to plunder and spared the people, so Sichuan was taken over at the very lowest cost; yet within the court the treatment of meritorious officials and surrendered commanders turned unbalanced, and with the players of the stage meddling in state affairs and slander flying, Guo Chongtao was killed in the first year of Tiansheng. A commander-in-chief dying on slander was a clear harbinger of the disintegration of the Later Tang state. After Li Cunxu's death the mutiny of Zhao Zaili and Li Siyuan's seizure of the throne came in succession, the most disorderly stretch of the Five Dynasties began, and Shu once more became the rear and the battlefield of the fighting in the north. Culturally, the block printing, the Buddhist statuary, the music and dance and the community of scholars that Sichuan had accumulated since the end of Tang partly flowed into the central plains around this transfer of power, and the murals and pottery figures of the Yongling tomb of Wang Jian remain today one of the most important material records of life in the Shu court.
result: 九二五年十一月，郭崇韜前鋒入成都，王衍出降，前蜀亡。蜀軍未嘗有全線崩潰的會戰，多數部隊在停戰與受降之間自動解體；郭崇韜入城即封府庫、禁剝掠、撫循百姓，遣將分守州郡，並受命為西川節度使坐鎮成都，主導善後。蜀地州縣自此由後唐直接置官，前蜀軍政合一的體制告終；王衍與其官屬被押送京師，授以虛職，遷於陳州一帶，其後終為所殺；郭崇韜亦在一年多後以叛逆之名被誅，兩位左右此役成敗的人先後不得善終，成為晚唐五代「功臣無罪而族滅」的一例。九之後蜀中軍亂起，孟知祥收拾舊部，建立後蜀，前蜀、後蜀前後相承共五十九年，直到後蜀廣政十八年為宋所滅，蜀地才再度歸入中原。此役因此不只是兩家政權的更替，更是蜀地歸屬的一次定案：以速度取蜀、以軍紀安蜀的經驗，成為此後中原王朝處理蜀地時反覆被援引的範例。
resultEn: In the eleventh month of 925 Guo Chongtao's vanguard entered Chengdu and Wang Yan came out to surrender; Former Shu was gone. The Shu army never fought a general pitched battle in which it was destroyed; most of its units dissolved between the armistice and the surrender. Guo sealed the treasury on entering the city, forbade plunder, soothed the people, sent officers to hold the prefectures, and was appointed military commissioner of Xichuan to sit at Chengdu and direct the settlement. From then on the prefectures of Shu were administered by officials appointed directly by Later Tang, and the fusion of civil and military authority that had characterised Former Shu came to an end. Wang Yan and his officials were sent to the capital, given titular offices and moved to the Chuzhou region, and he was eventually killed; Guo Chongtao too was executed a little over a year later on a charge of treason, so that the two men who had decided the outcome of this campaign both met bad ends, another instance in the late Tang and Five Dynasties of a meritorious servant destroyed without a legal charge. Nine years later a mutiny broke out in Sichuan, Meng Zhixiang gathered up the old troops and founded Later Shu, and Former and Later Shu together lasted fifty-nine years, until Later Shu was destroyed by Song in the eighteenth year of Guangzheng and Sichuan once more returned to the central plains. The campaign was therefore not merely a change of one house for another: it was a verdict on where Shu belonged, and the experience of taking Shu by speed and securing it by discipline became a model that later central plains dynasties kept citing whenever they had to deal with Shu.
